lawyer:
Khandaker Mahbubuddin Ahmed, Senior Advocate, instructed by Sharifuddin Chaklader, Advocate-on-Record -For the Petitioner. 	
Rafique-ul Huq, Senior Advocate, instructed by Md Nawab Ali, Advocate-on-Record -For the Respondents.

Haider Ali Miah (Md) ------ Petitioner
Vs.

full_judgment:
2. The short fact leading to this petition is that, plaintiff-petitioner instituted Title Suit No. 95 of 2001 in the 5th Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka for a declaration that charge-sheet dated 7-6-2001 issued by defendant No. 1 and signed by defendant No. 3 is illegal, void, inoperative and it has no legal effect and the same is not binding upon the plaintiff and no proceeding can be drawn up and proceeded on the basis of alleged charge-sheet and also for other reliefs. Further case of the plaintiff is that, he joined defendant Bank in 1984 and was ultimately promoted to the post of Assistant Vice President in the year 1998 Thereafter, due to his personal difficulties he tendered resignation on 12-4-2000 to the defendant-Bank which was done in accordance with the service rule. The plaintiff also wanted to know from his employer about any liability he may have in the bank and the bank replied in the negative. Thereafter, the plaintiff handed over his charge of the office on 9-3-2000 and he was given clearance from all sections and also obtained balance confirmation service from the Bank and after acceptance of the resignation by issuing release order from the bank he is no longer and no more in service and the plaintiff is entitled to get his all arrear dues as per rule. Thereafter, on 14-6-2001 the plaintiff received a charge-sheet containing certain fictitious allegations and was asked to submit his written reply and also asked to show cause why disciplinary action including dismissal from service shall not betaken against him. Thereafter, the plaintiff filed the present suit wherein an application under Order XXXIX rules 1 and 2 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure was filed praying for temporary injunction restraining the defendants from initiating any proceeding against him on the basis of charge-sheet dated 7-6-2001. The plaintiffs prayer for temporary injunction was rejected by the trial Court by order dated 1-7-2001. Against that order the plaintiff filed FMAT No. 673 of 2001 before the High Court Division which was rejected summarily by a Division Bench by order dated 8th August, 2001. Thereafter, the plaintiff preferred this petition before this Division. 

 3. Khandaker Mahbubuddin Ahmed, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner, submits that there being no provision in the service rule of the defendant Bank authorizing them to initiate disciplinary proceeding against a released employee or ex-employee so, initiation of the disciplinary proceeding against the plaintiff-petitioner is without jurisdiction. Further, he submits that the plaintiff-petitioner was released from service on 20-6-2000 and he is no longer an employee of the bank and therefore the service rule is not applicable to the plaintiff. As the petitioner has already resigned from the bank and he has been released he cannot be subjected to any disciplinary proceeding by the defendant bank but, in spite of that, the defendant bank proceeded with the disciplinary proceeding against him. The learned Advocate contended that if the defendant bank is not prevented in proceeding with the disciplinary action pending disposal of the suit the plaintiff will suffer irreparable loss and there shall arise multiplicity of suits and proceedings. 

 5. Mr. Rafique-ul Huq, learned Advocate entering caveat, on the other hand, submits that in the suit as framed by the plaintiff there cannot be any order of injunction as the plaintiff failed to make out any prima facie case for issuance of an injunction under Order XXXIX rules 1 and 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 6. We have gone through the judgment of the High Court Division and other available materials and we find no force in the argument advanced by Mr. Khandaker Mahbubuddin Ahmed for the petitioner. The High Court Division as well as the trial Court has not committed any illegality and wrong in dismissing the plaintiff’s prayer for temporary injunction. Furthermore, the plaintiff also failed to point out any ingredient required for issuing an injunction in such a case.
